recipes.name: Fried Chicken with Creamy Gravy
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 pound) whole chicken, cut into pieces

steps.text: In a medium bowl, beat together 1/2 cup milk and egg. In a resealable plastic bag, mix together the flour, garlic salt, paprika, pepper and poultry seasoning. Place chicken in bag, seal, and shake to coat. Dip chicken in milk and egg mixture, then once more in flour mixture. Reserve any remaining flour mixture.

In a large skillet, heat oil to 365 degrees F (185 degrees C). Place coated chicken in the hot oil, and brown on all sides. Reduce heat to medium-low, and continue cooking chicken until tender, about 30 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet, and drain on paper towels.

Discard all but 2 tablespoons of the frying oil. Over low heat, stir in 2 tablespoons of the reserved flour mixture. Stirring constantly, cook about 2 minutes. Whisk in chicken stock, scraping browned bits off bottom of skillet. Stir in 1 cup milk, and bring all to a boil over high heat, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to low, and simmer for about 5 minutes. Serve immediately with the chicken.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Chicken with Creamy Gravy
raw_recipe.description: Seasoned fried chicken with a rich gravy made from the pan drippings. Down home goodness.

review.reviewBody: Wow! This is amazing. A lot of people complimented on how amazing the gravy was, but I thought the chicken took the prize. I substituted garlic salt for garlic powder and added onion salt and I doubled the spices. I felt 3 cups of oil was way too much, so I used 1 1/2 cups and it was fine; I just flipped the chicken pieces as it was cooking. I also doubled the gravy and served it over mashed potatoes. It was to die for.

GINA, YOU HAVE GOT TO BE A COUNTRYSOUTHERN COOK! I KNOW A GOOD SOUTHERN RECIPE WHEN I TASTE IT :) FOR THOSE OF YOU WHO THINK THIS IS BLAND , TRY A SEASONED FLOUR SUCH AS KENTUCKY KERNEL. ANOTHER THING IS, I READ WHERE ONE REVIEWER THOUGHT THE RECIPE CALLED FOR TOO MUCH OIL TO COOK THE CHICKEN IN. I BELIEVE THAT THROUGH TRIAL AND ERROR YOU WILL FIND THAT IF YOU FOLLOW GINA'S RECIPE AND USE THE OIL CALLED FOR , YOU WILL GET THE ULTIMATE CRISPY FRIED CHICKEN THAT WILL STILL BE JUICY ON THE INSIDE.I WOULD LIKE TO ADD THAT I ENJOYED TRYING SOMEONE ELSES RECIPE AND HAVING IT TURN OUT SOOOO DELICIOUS!!! THANKS GINA!!

This is the best fried chicken I've ever made. For the simple reasons being that I doubled the spices, used a cast iron skillet, and soaked the chicken overnight in milk (with some apple cider vinegar in it). I rinsed off the milk & patted dry with paper towels. Another key is to not have the chicken too cold so I left it out for about 30 minutes after drying it. This way it doesn't bring the temperature of the oil down and you have a nice crispy coating. The gravy was over the moon good too! I made skillet biscuits before frying the chicken too. And an apple skillet cake before that in the morning. It was a wonderful Sunday Skillet Supper!

My first time making fried chicken and it turned out great! I only did a few modifications on the recommendation of my friend. I used boneless skinless chicken breast which I pounded to about 1.5 inches thick so it would cook evenly, and buttermilk instead of milk. Also, I coated the chicken in the seasoned flour mixture, then the milk and egg mixture, then back in the seasoned flour. I wanted to make sure the chicken was cooked all the way through so after frying I tossed them in the over to cook the rest of the way. Chicken was moist and flavorful. My whole family and our friends that were over raved about it. Definitely a keeper.

BEAT'S KFC HANDS DOWN! TO DIE 4 ! FOOLPROOF! SOUTHERN FRIED AT IT'S BEST! We love fried chicken but no matter what I tried it was either overdone,dry,or pink. Until I ran across this recipe! IT'S THE BOMB ! My husband LOVED IT! CRISPY, JUICY, & NO PINK! 
I read the reviews and made some changes: 
Soaked the chicken pieces in salt H2o at least 2-4 hours b4 cooking. (plan on the buttermilk soak someone suggested next time) I use a deep dish for the flour mix, it seems to stick better 4 me & I always double dip. I changed the amount of flour & seasonings to:

2 1/2 C Pancake mix instead of the flour. 2 T Garlic Powder. 1 T Paprika. 1 T pepper. 1 T salt. 2 t poultry seasoning. I cooked it in a heavy bottomed stock pot (no grease splatters), in Hot oil till golden honey color, then cooked it in 300* oven on a lightly greased cookie sheet for 35 minutes.
Cant thank you enough 4 sharing your recipe! We'll b having fried chicken more often now.

Excellent! This is almost how hubby makes fried chicken. He seasons both, the chicken and the flour, uses garlic powder rather than garlic salt and Lawrey's Seasoned Salt instead of paprika and poultry seasoning. Best fried chicken.

This was really really good. The chicken was super moist and the gravy was a TOTAL win. Two tips: I used twice as much spice as called for as the amount that actually ends up on the chicken isn't too much. Also, I made twice as much gravy so I had yummy leftovers. My first time making fried chicken and I felt like a total pro. Don't use less oil as people have suggested. The amount is needed to cook it right. Also, I only did it ten minutes per side and it was perfectly cooked.

This was one of the best fried chicken I have ever had. I am a southern cook and love flavorful food. I did not make the gravy (although I can't wait to try it) b/c I made baked mac n cheese with the chicken opposed to mashed potatoes. I used all chicken breast and split them in halves. What I did different was soaked my chicken in buttermilk and salt for about 5/6 hours and instead of using garlic salt and poultry season in the flour mixture, I used garlic powder and season all along with the other recommended ingredients. I'm sure I used more spices than what was required as I didn't measure, I only eyed it up. The chicken breast was so very juicy and didn't taste greasy. This is my new found way that I will fry my chicken.
This was so easy and so fast! I used chicken tenderloins, so it cooked in about half the time. Also, I used less oil and it worked perfectly. Love this!!

This recipe is what taught me how to make fried chicken! My husband loves this dish! For the gravy I usually sauté finely chopped onions in butter first until soften then add some fresh sage and follow the rest of the recipe. Thanks so much for sharing this gem of a recipe!
I cheated and used Washington chicken breading mix in place of the flour mixture, but otherwise I followed the recipe verbatim and it came out delicious!
Prefer my own fried chicken.
OK wow it's from above the rest love it and will treat my family with the best you have a great pallet thank you 😊

Recipe is great for beginners that want to make fried chicken for the first time. But the seasoning needs to be doubled if not tripled, or else the chicken will always come out bland. This Recipe will need to be adjusted to your personnel taste.

Nice and crispy! I made drumsticks, so it did not take as long as the recipe called for. I didn't use my thermometer on the oil, so the chicken was a little dark, but delicious. The gravy was nice. The only problem was that I used garlic powder instead of garlic salt, so a little bland. But my husband loved it!
One of the Best recipes I have made!

Made chicken fried chicken instead of fried chicken and was really good. Added rosemary to the seasoning and hammered the chicken with a cook time of 4 minutes per side. Need to thicken the sauce more
A huge hit! Poultry seasoning is the key to this recipe. It really gives it great flavor! ?? ??

My boyfriend is from Kentucky and KNOWS good fried chicken. He couldn't stop raving about this recipe! I used about 3/4 the amount of flour and doubled up on all the spices. For the gravy, instead of the flour mixture, I used a chicken gravy packet with milk and chicken broth and pan drippings. So delicious! Perfectly crispy and juicy!! Definitely my new go to fried chicken!
